examples.en: I'll send you the contract by email.

examples.ko: 계약서 송부 일정을 확인하고 싶은데 담당자께 문의해도 될까요?
examples.en: I'd like to check the schedule for sending the contract. May I ask the person in charge?
One document is missing from the list of papers to send.
The documents haven't been sent yet.

examples.ko: 자료를 먼저 송부하신 뒤에 전화 주세요.
examples.en: Please call me after you send the materials first.

examples.ko: 어제 송부한 파일이 열리지 않는다고 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a message that the file I sent yesterday won't open.

explain: '보내다'의 업무용·공문서 말투예요. 서류, 자료, 계약서처럼 격식 있는 물건에 쓰고, 친구에게 사진을 보낼 때는 '보내다'가 자연스러워요. 메일이나 공문에서 '송부드립니다'로 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I will send you the materials by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업무 메일이나 전화에서 정중하게 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely promise something in work emails or calls.

phrases.en: I received the documents yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 쪽에서 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the receiving side in a formal way.

phrases.en: I sent the photo to my friend right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말로, 격식 없는 상황에 알맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word, suitable for informal situations.

explain_en: It is the business and official-document version of '보내다'. It is used for formal items such as documents, materials and contracts, while sending a photo to a friend sounds natural only with '보내다'. You'll often see it in emails and notices as '송부드립니다'.

examples.en: My team leader approved my leave.
The company will approve the new budget.
The card company approved the payment.

examples.ko: 부모님이 승인하면 학생이 앱을 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If a parent approves, the student can use the app.
The person who approves it is not at their desk now.

examples.ko: 위원회가 승인한 약만 팔 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only medicine that the committee approved can be sold.

explain: '허락하다'는 누구나 쓰는 말이고, '승인하다'는 서류·예산·결제처럼 정해진 절차를 거쳐 허락할 때 써요. 받는 쪽은 '승인되다'를 써요. 반대말은 '거부하다'예요.

phrases.en: Please approve my vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락하는 사람에게 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to the person who gives approval.

phrases.en: I got approval from my team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락받는 사람의 입장에서 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation from the viewpoint of the person receiving permission.

phrases.en: The company rejected the request.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승인하다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 승인하다.

explain_en: '허락하다' is for any permission, while '승인하다' is for approval through a set procedure, such as documents, budgets, or payments. The receiving side uses '승인되다'. The opposite is '거부하다'.

dis.h: officially approve a plan or request
gh: formal; agree to a request or proposal
boss signs off on a document

p.n: The other word is specifically a superior signing off on a document.

examples.en: I looked through old newspapers at the library.
To view the documents, you have to submit an application.
You can view the certificate online.
There is a rule that only employees view this material.

examples.ko: 자료를 열람하는 동안 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos while viewing the material.
Please sign after you look over the contract.

explain: '열람하다'는 도서관, 관공서, 회사처럼 정해진 곳에서 자료나 서류를 확인하며 읽는 거예요. '읽다'와 달리 허락이나 절차가 있다는 느낌이 있어요. '열람실', '열람 신청'처럼 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I study in the library reading room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료를 읽는 방을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common word for the room where materials are read.

phrases.en: I applied for access to view the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료를 보기 전에 허락을 받는 절차를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the step of asking permission before viewing materials.

phrases.example: 이 자료는 누구나 열람할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Anyone can view these materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: 볼 수 있도록 허락된 자료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for materials that people are allowed to see.

explain_en: '열람하다' is checking and reading materials or documents at a set place such as a library, public office, or company. Unlike '읽다', it suggests permission or procedure. Common terms: '열람실' (reading room), '열람 신청' (viewing request).

gh: read books as an activity; no object

p.n: The swap is everyday; the original sounds like officially viewing or checking records.

examples.ko: 이사회 소집 요구서에는 안건과 날짜가 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The request to convene the board listed the agenda and the date.
I sent the company a written request to change the contract.

examples.ko: 요구서에 서명한 사람이 백 명이 넘어요.
examples.en: More than a hundred people signed the written demand.
The parents submitted a written demand to the school.

examples.ko: 요구서 양식은 홈페이지에서 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can download the demand form from the website.
Who wrote this written demand?

explain: 상대에게 무엇을 해 달라고 공식적으로 적어 내는 문서예요. 회사, 노조, 단체 같은 곳에서 주로 쓰고, '요구서를 내다', '요구서를 제출하다', '요구서를 보내다'처럼 말해요. 개인의 일상에서는 '요구 사항'이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: The union submitted a written request to the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요구서를 내다'보다 공식적인 느낌이 있어서 회사나 단체 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more formal than 'to hand in a request'; it suits talk about companies and organizations.

phrases.example: 회사는 어제 학부모 단체의 요구서를 받았어요.
phrases.en: The company received a written request from the parents' group yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요구서를 보내는 쪽이 아니라 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one who receives the request, not the one who sends it.

phrases.en: I wrote the necessary details in the written request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요구서 안에 어떤 내용을 쓰는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what content you put inside the request letter.
phrases.en_equiv: to write in a request letter

explain_en: It is a document officially written to ask the other side to do something. It is mostly used by companies, unions and groups, in forms like '요구서를 내다', '요구서를 제출하다' and '요구서를 보내다'. In personal daily life, '요구 사항' is more common.

examples.ko: 저는 모르는 것이 있으면 선생님께 도움을 요청해요.
examples.en: If there's something I don't know, I ask the teacher for help.
I asked the hotel for more towels.
If you need it, ask anytime.
I don't really know how to make a request.

examples.ko: 다시 한번 설명해 달라고 요청하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to ask them to explain once more.
I sent the documents you requested by email today.

explain: 가까운 사이에는 '부탁하다', 호텔·회사·이메일처럼 공식적인 상황에서는 '요청하다'를 써요. '요청 사항', '요청을 받다'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요. '요구하다'는 당연히 해 달라는 느낌이라 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I asked my friend to help me move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 사이에 도움을 청할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for asking for help among people who are close.

phrases.en: If a problem comes up, ask a staff member for help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 도움이 필요할 때 공식적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for formally asking for help.

phrases.example: 요청 사항이 있으면 여기에 써 주세요.
phrases.en: If you have any requests, please write them here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔이나 식당에서 원하는 것을 적는 칸에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on forms at hotels and restaurants for things you want.

explain_en: Between people who are close, use '부탁하다'; in formal settings like hotels, companies and emails, use '요청하다'. The noun appears in '요청 사항' (requests) and '요청을 받다' (receive a request). '요구하다' is stronger, as if demanding something owed.

p.n: 부탁하다 sounds like a personal favor, less formal than 요청하다.

examples.en: I had my graduation thesis bound at a print shop.
Please bind this report with a spiral.
It takes about a day to get it bound.

examples.ko: 인쇄한 종이를 모아서 직접 제본해서 책처럼 만들었어요.
examples.en: I gathered the printed pages and bound them myself to make a book.
Check the page numbers before binding.

examples.ko: 제본한 책은 오래 두어도 잘 안 흩어져요.
examples.en: A bound book doesn't fall apart easily even if you keep it for a long time.

explain: 낱장의 종이를 묶어서 책이나 논문, 보고서로 만들 때 써요. 보통 복사집이나 인쇄소에 '제본 맡기다'라고 하고, '스프링 제본'처럼 방식을 앞에 붙여 말해요.

phrases.en: I left the binding with the copy shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 하지 않고 가게에 부탁할 때 '제본을 맡기다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say 제본을 맡기다 when you ask a shop to do the binding instead of doing it yourself.

phrases.en: I gave the bound report to the professor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제본한'이 보고서나 논문 앞에 와서 묶여 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a report or thesis, 제본한 describes it as already bound.

phrases.en: Please contact me when the binding is done.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묶는 작업이 다 끝났다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the binding work is finished.

explain_en: It is used when binding loose sheets into a book, thesis or report. People usually say '제본 맡기다' at a copy shop or print shop, and put the method in front, as in '스프링 제본'.

examples.ko: 계약서를 조속히 검토해서 오늘 안에 의견을 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll review the contract promptly and give you my opinion today.
Please handle it promptly after checking.
I hope this problem gets resolved quickly.
To save the patient, the response has to be swift.
Thank you for giving a prompt and accurate answer.

examples.ko: 일 처리가 조속하지 않아서 고객이 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The work wasn't handled quickly, so the customer got angry.

explain: '조속히' 형태로 많이 쓰고, 이메일이나 공문, 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 상황에서 '빨리' 대신 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 어색하니까 '빨리'를 쓰세요.

phrases.en: Please resolve the problem quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공문이나 이메일에서 빠른 처리를 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in official letters or emails to request quick action.

phrases.en: I'll contact you promptly once it's confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빨리'보다 격식 있는 말이라 업무 연락에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than '빨리'; suits business messages.

phrases.en: This work needs to be finished as soon as possible.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 빨리 마쳐야 한다는 뜻의 격식 있는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say a task must be finished soon.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '조속히' and replaces '빨리' in formal settings such as emails, official letters and news. It sounds stiff when talking with friends, so use '빨리' there.

examples.ko: 선생님은 학생들에게 안전 규칙을 다시 주지시켰어요.
examples.en: The teacher made the students fully aware of the safety rules again.

examples.ko: 회사는 직원들에게 보안 수칙을 주지시키기 위해 교육을 열었어요.
examples.en: The company held training to make staff aware of the security rules.

examples.ko: 아이에게 위험한 곳을 반복해서 주지시켜야 해요.
examples.en: You have to make a child firmly aware of dangerous places, repeatedly.

examples.ko: 규칙을 모두에게 주지시킨 뒤에 시험을 시작했어요.
examples.en: We started the exam after making sure everyone knew the rules.
I tried to get the changed schedule across with a notice.

examples.ko: 먼저 책임이 무엇인지 분명하게 주지시키고 싶어요.
examples.en: First, I want to make clear what the responsibility is.

explain: 주지시키다는 이미 있는 사실이나 규칙을 모두가 확실히 알게 할 때 써서 안내·교육·공지 이야기에 어울려요. 처음 알려 주는 것은 '알리다', 다시 알려서 기억하게 하는 것은 '상기시키다'예요. 딱딱한 말이라 일상에서는 '다시 알려 주다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 아이들에게 길에서 지켜야 할 규칙을 주지시켜야 해요.
phrases.en: We must make sure children understand the rules to follow on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 알게 해야 하는 일을 말할 때 자주 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common ending for things people must be made to know.

phrases.example: 회사는 직원들에게 안전 수칙을 철저히 주지시켜요.
phrases.en: The company makes sure employees thoroughly understand the safety rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠뜨리는 사람이 없도록 모두 확실히 알게 한다는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning to make sure everyone knows without anyone being missed.

phrases.en: Please make the rules clear to everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱하지 않게 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, everyday way to say the same thing without sounding stiff.

explain_en: 주지시키다 fits notices, training and announcements: it means making sure everyone clearly knows an existing fact or rule. Telling someone for the first time is 알리다, and bringing something back to mind is 상기시키다. It is stiff, so in daily life 다시 알려 주다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: We will begin the ceremony once all the guests are seated.
Passengers, please take your seats.

examples.ko: 면접관이 착석하라고 말할 때까지 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I stood until the interviewer told me to be seated.
Everyone is seated, so let's begin now.

examples.ko: 회의실에 착석한 사람은 아직 세 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: Only three people have taken their seats in the meeting room so far.

examples.ko: 비행기가 뜨기 전에 모두 착석하셔야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone must be seated before the plane takes off.

explain: '앉다'보다 격식을 차린 말이라서 안내 방송, 행사, 면접 같은 자리에서 자주 들려요. 친구와 대화할 때 쓰면 딱딱하게 들려서 보통은 '앉다'라고 해요. '착석해 주세요'처럼 부탁하는 표현으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Please sit down comfortably.
phrases.nuance_ko: 착석하다보다 훨씬 자주 쓰는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common everyday word than 착석하다.

phrases.en: Guests, please take your seats.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내 방송이나 행사에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask in announcements and at events.

phrases.en: I'll start the presentation after everyone is seated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모두 앉은 다음에 할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what happens after everyone has sat down.

explain_en: It is a more formal word than '앉다', so you hear it in announcements, ceremonies and interviews. With friends it sounds stiff, so people usually just say '앉다'. A common pattern is the polite request '착석해 주세요'.

examples.en: I attach a photo file to the email.
I will send the application together with the documents attached.
I forgot to attach the file.
It is better if you attach a resume to the application.
I attached a simple map at the very bottom of the mail.
Please open the attached document.

explain: '첨부 파일'처럼 이메일에서 쓰는 말이에요. 파일을 붙여 보내는 상황에 쓰고, 풀이나 테이프로 붙일 때는 '붙이다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 메일에 있는 첨부 파일을 열어 보세요.
phrases.en: Please open the attached file in the email.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이메일에 붙여 보낸 파일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A file attached to an email.

phrases.en: A photo is attached to the email.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 붙어 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something that is already attached.

phrases.en: Please attach a photo to the application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 붙여 달라고 정중하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to attach something.

explain_en: It appears in '첨부 파일' (attachment) in email. Use it for attaching files; for sticking something with glue or tape, use '붙이다'.
